lineup:C:4035538:w1.title: David Montgomery had the Week 1 you wanted
lineup:C:4035538:w1.text: James Cook III got the Week 1 nod at running back while David Montgomery racked up a near-30-point day on your bench. One early swap and that week looks a lot better.

pos:K1:FLEX6.title: Your kicker is an all-star. Your flex spot, less so.
pos:K1:FLEX6.text: Top kicker production in the league, dead last at flex, the wild-card spot. Funny sport where the guy kicking field goals is outperforming the guy catching touchdowns.

lineup:B:4259545:w1.title: D'Andre Swift's best day happened in street clothes
lineup:B:4259545:w1.text: Emeka Egbuka got the Week 1 flex nod while D'Andre Swift quietly had one of the best bench days in the league. Nearly everything else on your sheet, you got right.

pos:WR1:K8.title: Your receivers are the best in the league. Your kicker, not so much.
pos:WR1:K8.text: Wide receiver points, first in the league. Kicker points, dead last. The waiver wire's full of guys who kick, if you ever feel like upgrading the least glamorous spot on your roster.

proj:over:4241389:4360248.title: CeeDee Lamb didn't get the ESPN memo
proj:over:4241389:4360248.text: Lamb keeps blowing past his weekly number like it's a suggestion. Kyle Pitts Sr. is coming in under his more often than not, the quieter story on the same roster.

lineup:C:4241416:w1.title: The Waddle bet, origin story
lineup:C:4241416:w1.text: Before the Waddle bet became a running joke, there was Week 1: Jaylen Waddle got the flex nod and mustered next to nothing while Chuba Hubbard quietly erupted on your bench. The bet lives on anyway.

pos:RB3:QB8.title: Quarterback is the one hole in an otherwise solid roster
pos:RB3:QB8.text: Running back ranks third in the league for you, no complaints there. Quarterback ranks dead last though, proof that even a solid roster needs one position to keep it humble.

proj:under:4258173:4572680.title: Nico Collins is outplaying his own scouting report
proj:under:4258173:4572680.text: Collins keeps topping his projection by a wide margin most weeks. Tucker Kraft's running a bit behind his, the one soft spot in an otherwise strong lineup.

lineup:D:4248528:w1.title: Christian Watson, still waiting for his shot
lineup:D:4248528:w1.text: Quinshon Judkins started at flex in Week 1 while Christian Watson put up one of the league's biggest bench performances right next to him. He's been doing that quietly all season. At some point the lineup card has to notice.

lineup:C:4432665:w3.title: The Brock Bowers decision still stings
lineup:C:4432665:w3.text: Dalton Schultz started at tight end in Week 3 while Brock Bowers put up one of the best bench days anyone had all season, on your own roster. That one's going to come up again.

pos:QB2:K7.title: Quarterback's strong. Kicker's an afterthought.
pos:QB2:K7.text: Your quarterback production ranks second in the league. Kicker ranks near the bottom, which is the least surprising sentence in this entire audit.

proj:over:4685472:4596448.title: Tetairoa McMillan is making ESPN look silly
proj:over:4685472:4596448.text: McMillan keeps clearing his projection by a wide margin most weeks. Bucky Irving's the opposite case, settling in under his more often than not.

lineup:B:5083076:w3.title: One tight end call away from perfect
lineup:B:5083076:w3.text: Week 3 is the only blemish here: Tyler Warren got the start at tight end while Harold Fannin Jr. piled up points from the bench. Everywhere else, you played it exactly right.

pos:RB1:WR8.title: Running back is doing the heavy lifting
pos:RB1:WR8.text: Your running backs lead the league, doing enough work for two positions. Your receivers rank dead last, so that's the shopping list if a name worth adding shows up on waivers.

proj:over:4430737:4870795.title: Kyren Williams has stopped listening to ESPN
proj:over:4430737:4870795.text: Kyren Williams keeps blowing past his projection every week, like the algorithm hasn't noticed. Makai Lemon's the opposite story, quietly coming in under his number.

pos:QB1:RB8.title: Quarterback's elite. Running back needs the help.
pos:QB1:RB8.text: Your quarterback room leads the entire league. Running back ranks dead last, mostly because the position lost its workhorse for the year. Still the clearest spot to upgrade.

proj:under:3918298:4429160.title: Josh Allen has carried this roster
proj:under:3918298:4429160.text: Allen keeps clearing his weekly number by a solid margin. Achane's season ended on a torn ACL, which is the real reason that side of the roster has struggled, not a projection miss.

lineup:B:15847:w2.title: Travis Kelce picked the wrong week to sit
lineup:B:15847:w2.text: Dallas Goedert started at tight end in Week 2 while Travis Kelce quietly piled up points from your bench. One swap away from a very different week.

pos:WR3:DST8.title: Receivers are solid. Defense is the real gap.
pos:WR3:DST8.text: Your wide receivers rank solidly in the top half of the league. Your defense ranks dead last, dragging the rest of the roster down like it's trying to make a point.
